segments: Chronography of Barhebraeus.
in Sarug,
some of his friends asked him,
"Where then is it pleasant for you,
here or there?" And he replied,
"Here the possessions are plentiful,
but honor we left behind in Qalʿah."
And in that same year, Sultan Qilij Arslan took the city of Ankara and Gangra from the Greeks.
And at this time, the Franks who were stationed in Egypt and in Alexandria for the collection of the gold tribute and the guarding of the gates,
sent to Amalric, king of Jerusalem,
saying, "This country is empty of troops,
and you are easily able to gain dominion over it."
And while all the nobles wished to go,
the king himself restrained them prudently, saying,
"All the gold of Egypt is already being gathered to us,
and if we march against it,
the Arabs, out of their hatred of us,
will incline more toward Nur al-Din,
and will send and bring him.
And war will come upon us from both within and without,
and we shall not succeed."
The nobles, however, were not persuaded by the counsel of the king,
but said,
"We will go and gain dominion over Egypt
before Nur al-Din can ready {or: gather} his forces to come."
And thus the king was overcome by them,
and they assembled,
and went in haste.
And they captured the city of Bilbais,
and plundered it and carried its population into captivity.
And they came and encamped against Cairo and Egypt (Fustat).
The Egyptians, however,
because they feared lest that which befell the people of Bilbais should befall them,
encouraged one another,
and took their places on the walls,
and valiantly held out in the battle with the Franks.
And also al-ʿAdid, the caliph of Egypt, cut off {OCR?} the locks of hair of his wives and his daughters,
and sent them to Nur al-Din and said,
"Behold, my women, in grief, are weeping and wailing and beseeching you to come to their aid
and rescue them from the hands of the Franks."
Nur al-Din lingered about two months gathering forces.
And when he delayed,
and the fighting grew fierce against Egypt,
Shawar, that vizier of Egypt, sent to Amalric and to the nobles of the Franks, saying,
"You know my affection toward you.
And if I knew that the Arabs would accept it from me that I surrender Egypt to you,
I would quickly surrender it to you.
